title: VEGA: Automatically Generating Compiler Backends using a Pre-trained Transformer Model
problem: Developing compiler backends for new hardware targets is time-consuming and requires deep expertise; each new target demands substantial manual engineering effort to customize compilation passes and code generation.
motivation: Accelerating compiler backend development reduces time-to-market for new architectures and enables faster deployment of DSA-specific compilers, democratizing compiler engineering.
method: VEGA organizes the functions (pieces of code) that compilers use into groups and creates customizable templates for each group. Using a pre-trained transformer (a type of machine learning model), it learns which parts of the templates are the same for all hardware and which parts differ depending on the hardware. VEGA then automatically generates compiler code for new hardware targets by filling in the templates with the hardware description, eliminating the need for manual engineering.
key_novelty: Using a pre-trained transformer (a machine learning model) to automatically generate compiler code from target descriptions, eliminating manual engineering work.
contributions: An AI-driven system (VEGA) for auto-generating compiler backends using pre-trained transformers
Function-template abstraction and feature extraction for target-specific customization
Demonstration on three targets (RISC-V, RI5CY with extensions, xCORE) generating backends in under one hour with 62-73% function accuracy
Confidence scoring for generated functions to guide minimal manual intervention
limitations: 30-40% of functions still require manual fixing; generalization to very different ISAs or complex extensions not demonstrated; transformer training data and scaling requirements not discussed.
